message.content: {"A0100":"A0100 most plausibly seeks to reduce exposure after committing a missile by converting its head-on, descending approach into a sustained hard right turn while its missile continues north; the ammunition decrease and simultaneous opposing launch support post-shot separation rather than continued direct closure.","A0200":"A0200 most plausibly seeks to maintain pressure and support its missile engagement by continuing the fast, descending northbound closure after expending a missile rather than breaking away; its path remains nearly aligned with the southbound opponents while A0100 turns sharply aside.","B0100":"B0100 most plausibly seeks to preserve head-on firing geometry and sustain pressure by accelerating southward in a steady descent, launching during the continuing closure and then remaining nose-on rather than separating as the opposing aircraft approach.","B0200":"B0200 most plausibly seeks an early head-on missile engagement while retaining pressure by maintaining its fast southbound descent through missile expenditure; despite A0100 launching at the same time and subsequently turning aside, B0200 continues closing almost directly toward Team A."}

{"A0100":"A0100 most plausibly seeks to reduce nose-on exposure after an earlier missile release by executing a sustained descending right break, then leveling eastbound; its missile is already outbound northward while opposing missiles advance south and curve east, and the maneuver rapidly creates lateral separation from the closing formation.","A0200":"A0200 most plausibly seeks first to preserve pressure behind its already-outbound missile by continuing the northbound descent, then to reduce direct exposure as the formations close by committing to a hard right turn; the late lateral displacement sacrifices head-on closure while retaining speed.","B0100":"B0100 most plausibly seeks to sustain its attack and keep favorable forward geometry by holding a nearly straight, accelerating southbound descent, given its missile is already ahead and both Team A aircraft are closing from the south; the absence of a defensive break suggests continued commitment despite opposing missiles in the corridor.","B0200":"B0200 most plausibly seeks to press the closest nose-on approach by maintaining an accelerating southbound descent toward Team A’s western side, with its own missile already ahead; the steadily shrinking separation and minimal lateral maneuver suggest attack continuation rather than an attempt to disengage from the inbound exchange."}

{"A0100":"A0100 most plausibly seeks post-launch standoff and reduced exposure by holding an accelerating eastward offset while its missile continues north toward the B formation; it maintains this separation after the missile disappears alongside B0200’s inactivation rather than turning back into the engagement.","A0200":"A0200 most plausibly seeks to survive the missile exchange by combining a sustained descending right turn with acceleration, creating lateral and vertical separation as both B missiles close from the north; it maintains this defensive displacement after B0200 becomes inactive rather than re-entering directly.","B0100":"B0100 most plausibly seeks to survive the incoming A-missile pass by changing from a straight southward descent into a hard, rolling southeast break as the missiles close on the B pair; it remains active after their removal and B0200’s simultaneous inactivation.","B0200":"B0200 most plausibly seeks to spoil the closing A missiles’ geometry by steepening its descent and entering a hard left break as both approach from the south near its altitude; the attempt does not preserve it, as it becomes inactive when both missiles are removed."}

{"A0100":"A0100 most plausibly seeks to re-enter the engagement against the lone active opponent by abandoning its long eastbound transit for a sustained hard left reversal and slight descent; B0100 remained several kilometres west, while the turn reduced their north-south offset and preserved A0100’s substantial altitude advantage.","A0200":"A0200 most plausibly seeks to survive the converging B01001 missile by sustaining a high-bank, descending turn from east toward northeast, generating lateral displacement rather than flying predictably ahead of B0100; the missile continued closing from the northwest while B0100 followed near A0200’s altitude.","B0100":"B0100 most plausibly seeks to continue pursuing A0200 after earlier missile expenditure by turning from southeast toward east and descending to nearly A0200’s altitude; the maneuver removes their north-south offset while B01001’s path also converges on A0200, consistent with sustained pressure rather than disengagement.","B0200":"B0200 remains inactive with invalid flight data throughout the window, so no tactical intention can be inferred."}

{"A0100":"A0100 most plausibly sought a firing solution on B0100 by descending through a sustained left turn that rapidly closed the lone opponent, then expending its last missile and reversing toward a right turn as the missile converged; B0100 and the missile became inactive together, consistent with completion of that attack.","A0200":"A0200 most plausibly sought to survive B0100’s already-airborne missile by maintaining high speed and arcing from northeast toward north, dragging the weapon without allowing meaningful closure rather than spending its own remaining missile; the threat continued following even after B0100 became inactive.","B0100":"B0100 most plausibly sought initially to sustain pressure behind its already-airborne missile by advancing northeast toward A0200, but after A0100 launched from the northeast it shifted into a steep climbing turn, apparently seeking vertical and lateral separation from the converging weapon; it became inactive when that missile was removed.","B0200":"B0200 remained inactive with no valid flight state throughout the window, so no tactical intention can be inferred."}
